nodes.line: I have got about four minutes before I am needed.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. I start at knock-off and for a month the Guildford back lane has had somebody in it who is not waiting for bread. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

You are the first person to stop all morning. A light on that lane costs Guildford $120 and the landlord has said no twice, so we are doing it ourselves. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Do not make a scene about it.
Alright. I am listening properly this time.

choices.text: The Lane Light, Guildford — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
Ah. Someone with two working legs.

Not being dramatic about this. The flour for Guildford comes off a truck at knock-off and last the week of the show the truck came and the flour did not. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. Ask for me by name at the counter.

I am told you do odd jobs. The Guildford loading zone has had a car in it at knock-off every morning this week and the driver waits in it, which makes it worse. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. Come back and tell me straight.
Say it plain and I will pay you plain.

choices.text: The Loading Zone, Guildford — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.

npcs.name: Jia, front of house at Guildford

nodes.line: You are early. Or late. I have lost track.

I'll be straight with you. Somebody two doors down from Guildford put up a sign on the week of the show that says the same six words as ours, in the same order. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Do that and we're square.

It has been three weeks. This business was at Yennora before it was at Guildford, and there is a woman there who still has the original book. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I will owe you one, and I pay those.
I had a feeling. Go on.

choices.text: The Sourdough Sign, Guildford — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
Been here since before it was like this. Go on.

You are the first person to stop all morning. We are running a stall for Green Square on the long weekend and a stall needs $103 of gear that nobody has volunteered to pay for. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Do not make a scene about it.
Take a breath. Then say the whole thing.

choices.text: The Green Square Pool — that's done.
The Petition Stall, Green Square — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.

npcs.name: Esteban, swim coach at Green Square

nodes.line: Do not mind the mess. It is structural now.

Not being dramatic about this. I coach 76 kids at Green Square at twenty past four and three of them have stopped coming without anybody ringing me. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. Ask for me by name at the counter.

I am told you do odd jobs. A group has been coming over the Green Square fence after close and swimming in the dark, which is how Green Square loses its pool. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. Come back and tell me straight.
Go on then. What did you find.

choices.text: The Deep End, Green Square — that's done.

nodes.line: If you are selling something the answer is no.

I'll be straight with you. The kiosk at Green Square has a roll of raffle tickets in it and a freezer that has been running warm since the long weekend. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Do that and we're square.

It has been three weeks. They want everyone from Green Square to drive to the new centre at Erskineville, so somebody should go and see whether it is any good. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Evangelos, taxi driver at Chester Hill

nodes.line: Cash only and no, I am joking. What do you want.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. The rank outside Chester Hill used to hold nine cars and since a wet Monday it holds four, and nobody will say who moved the line. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

You are the first person to stop all morning. Since the rank at Chester Hill shrank I am $143 a week down, and the association wants that number from somebody who can prove it. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Do not make a scene about it.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.

choices.text: The Chester Hill Rank — that's done.
Lost Fares, Chester Hill — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.

npcs.name: Bo, rank marshal at Chester Hill

nodes.line: You have got a face like you can keep your mouth shut.

Not being dramatic about this. Cars that have never sat in the Chester Hill queue turn up at ten past five and take the front of it, and the drivers who waited say nothing. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. Ask for me by name at the counter.

I am told you do odd jobs. When the last train into Chester Hill is late, 45 people come out at once and I have to have cars there before they do. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. Come back and tell me straight.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.

nodes.line: Right. Talk while I do this.

I'll be straight with you. I have stood on this door near Chester Hill for 45 years and since a wet Monday somebody has been sending my guests to a different rank. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Do that and we're square.

It has been three weeks. The plates working the Chester Hill rank are dispatched from a depot at Sefton, and the man who runs it has never met a driver he liked. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I will owe you one, and I pay those.
Well? I can read your face from here.
